automotive-ev-battery.title: Massive recall in China affects Tesla, Xiaomi and others
automotive-ev-battery.summary: China has launched its largest automotive recall action to date, affecting several million vehicles from Tesla, Xiaomi, Leapmotor, Xpeng, and Zeekr due to potential issues with mechanical emergency door unlocking systems. This recalls significant safety and regulatory implications for major EV manufacturers operating in the Chinese market.

automotive-ev-battery.title: TU Graz researchers boost lithium titanate conductivity through 'hole punching' crystal lattice
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Researchers at TU Graz have significantly increased the ionic conductivity of lithium titanate by deliberately introducing defects into the material's crystal lattice structure, activating new pathways for lithium ions. This breakthrough could enhance the performance of lithium titanate as a battery anode material with potential applications in next-generation EV batteries.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Genesis unveils GV90 luxury electric SUV
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Hyundai Motor Group's luxury brand Genesis unveiled the GV90, a full-sized electric SUV that represents the largest model in the entire group. The vehicle will be the first produced at Hyundai's new dedicated EV manufacturing facility in Ulsan, South Korea.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Princeton Critical Minerals Raises $16M to Scale Lithium Production Technologies
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Princeton Critical Minerals, a University of Pennsylvania spinout, has secured $16 million in funding to expand its brine-based lithium production platform across the United States and South America. The capital injection aims to accelerate commercial deployments of the company's technology for increasing lithium yields from brine sources.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Tatra Trucks electrifies its first off-road truck
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Czech commercial vehicle manufacturer Tatra Trucks has unveiled its first all-electric truck, the Force e-Drive BEV, featuring a 480 kWh battery, all-wheel drive, and up to 550 kW of power. The 8x8 prototype is engineered for demanding applications in construction and mining sectors.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Hyundai starts taking orders for $17,700 Ioniq V, but you can't have it
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Hyundai has begun accepting pre-sale orders for its upcoming Ioniq V, a competitively priced electric vehicle, though availability remains restricted to non-English speaking markets at present. The $17,700 starting price positions the model as an affordable EV option in the global market.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Hypercharge launches home charging rewards programme
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Canadian EV charging firm Hypercharge has introduced a new home charging programme offering eligible drivers a complimentary Level 2 charger in exchange for participation in a reward scheme. The initiative aims to incentivize residential EV charging adoption.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Toyota Is Still Working On That Futuristic Fluoride-Ion EV Battery
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Toyota continues development of next-generation fluoride-ion EV batteries while simultaneously expanding its electrified vehicle portfolio in the U.S. market. The company is pursuing both near-term commercialization of conventional EVs and long-term battery technology innovation.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Xiaomi posts further loss in Q2 with its EV division
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Xiaomi's Smart EV division recorded an operating loss of 2.6 billion yuan in the second quarter of 2026 despite significantly higher vehicle deliveries. The deficit has narrowed compared to the first quarter, indicating progress toward profitability.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Legal battle forms around Polestar's US exit
automotive-ev-battery.summary: A New Jersey Polestar dealer has filed a lawsuit challenging the manufacturer's exit from the U.S. new car market, alleging that the Connected Vehicle Rule is merely a pretext for withdrawal. The legal dispute highlights tensions between regulatory compliance and business strategy in the EV sector.

world-news.title: Iran war live: Trump says he views Strait of Hormuz as 'American territory'
world-news.summary: US President Trump made controversial statements regarding the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global shipping route, while commenting on Iran negotiations. The remarks escalate geopolitical tensions in a region vital to international energy supplies and maritime commerce.

world-news.title: Russian double-tap drone strike kills 15 in Ukrainian mall, officials say
world-news.summary: Russian forces conducted a double-tap drone strike on a shopping center in Ukraine, killing at least 15 people and injuring over 130, including 23 children. The attack represents continued escalation in Russia's aerial campaign against Ukrainian civilian infrastructure.

world-news.title: Israel re-establishes closed West Bank settlement, defying growing international protests
world-news.summary: Israel has re-established a West Bank settlement with 30 families amid nationalist sentiment, despite widespread international opposition and Palestinian concerns. The move represents a significant escalation in Israeli settlement policy with major implications for Israeli-Palestinian relations.

world-news.title: UK, Canada and Australia condemn Israel for refusing criminal probe into aid worker killings in Gaza
world-news.summary: Three Western nations have condemned Israel's refusal to conduct a criminal investigation into an Israeli strike that killed seven World Central Kitchen humanitarian workers in Gaza. The diplomatic rebuke highlights international concerns over accountability for civilian casualties in the conflict.

world-news.title: Myanmar military bombing kills 14 at Buddhist monastery, opposition reports
world-news.summary: Myanmar's military conducted a bombing attack on a Buddhist monastery during a religious retreat, killing at least 14 people. The strike underscores the ongoing civil conflict in Myanmar and the military's continued targeting of civilian areas.

world-news.title: Hong Kong's Tiananmen activists guilty in national security trial
world-news.summary: Three Hong Kong activists were found guilty of inciting subversion of state power under China's National Security Law imposed on the territory. The conviction represents a significant development in Beijing's enforcement of security legislation and restrictions on political freedoms in Hong Kong.

world-news.title: Germany investigates Russia links to weapons cache discovered in woods, reports say
world-news.summary: German intelligence is investigating a cache of weapons found in the country, alleging they were part of a Russian operation to carry out assassinations. The discovery highlights escalating security tensions between NATO members and Russia.

world-news.title: Ebola vaccine trial to start in DR Congo as warning issued over speed of infections
world-news.summary: A vaccine trial is commencing in the Democratic Republic of Congo as health authorities warn of rapidly accelerating Ebola transmission, with half of 2,500 recorded deaths occurring in the previous 20 days. The outbreak represents a significant global health emergency requiring international response.

world-news.title: Mexico Governor Ruben Rocha returns to office despite US criminal charges
world-news.summary: Mexico's Sinaloa state governor resumed office despite facing criminal accusations from the Trump administration alleging ties to drug cartels. The development underscores ongoing bilateral tensions between the US and Mexico over narcotics trafficking and governance.

world-news.title: US debt tops $40 trillion, Americans left with the bill
world-news.summary: The United States national debt has exceeded $40 trillion for the first time in history and continues accelerating. The milestone underscores significant macroeconomic challenges with potential implications for global financial markets and US economic policy.

science-space.title: Trump signs new national space policy to enable 1,000 US rocket launches per year
science-space.summary: The United States has updated its national space policy to significantly expand domestic spaceflight capabilities, targeting more than 1,000 rocket launches annually by 2030. This policy modernization reflects a major shift in how the nation manages spaceflights and reentries to support increased launch cadence.

science-space.title: Japan unveils Mars moon sample-return spacecraft ahead of Oct. 19 launch
science-space.summary: Japan has revealed its MMX spacecraft ahead of its October 19 launch, which will conduct a sample-return mission to Phobos, one of Mars's moons. The mission represents a significant international effort to collect and return material from the Martian system to Earth.

science-space.title: 'Dark stars' could be the seeds of supermassive black holes, scientists say
science-space.summary: Scientists have proposed that mysterious dark stars may have served as the seeds for supermassive black holes, with evidence potentially found in gravitational wave signals permeating the cosmos. This discovery could fundamentally reshape our understanding of how the universe's most massive objects formed.

science-space.title: Webb Opens Treasure Chest
science-space.summary: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has captured detailed infrared images of the Carina Nebula's 'Treasure Chest,' a cometary globule representing an isolated cloud of gas and dust. The observation provides unprecedented insights into star-forming regions and the structures within them.

science-space.title: NASA Shares Views of August Solar Eclipse from Ground, Air, Space
science-space.summary: NASA researchers and photographers captured observations of the August 12 total solar eclipse visible from Greenland, Iceland, and Spain, documenting the Sun's corona from multiple vantage points. The eclipse provided valuable data for studying solar atmospheric phenomena.

science-space.title: What happens when a galaxy's supermassive black hole turns off? These dying radio galaxies could show us
science-space.summary: Astronomers have identified a previously unknown population of galaxies with fading radio lobes, revealing the fate of massive outflows when their central black hole engines shut down. This discovery advances understanding of black hole activity and galactic evolution cycles.

science-space.title: NASA's Artemis II Crew Set to Receive Congressional Space Medal of Honor
science-space.summary: President Trump will award the Congressional Space Medal of Honor to the four-member Artemis II crew—NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, plus Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen—during a ceremony at Johnson Space Center on August 28. The ceremony recognizes their historic lunar flyby mission.

science-space.title: SpaceX fires up Starship ahead of megarocket's 1st orbital flight
science-space.summary: SpaceX has completed a single-engine test-firing of its Starship spacecraft as preparation for its first orbital test flight. The successful engine test marks a significant milestone in the development of the next-generation fully reusable launch system.

science-space.title: TB 26-04 Updates and Modernization of NASA's Chemical Equilibrium with Applications (CEA) Code
science-space.summary: NASA has updated its Chemical Equilibrium with Applications code, a foundational tool for propulsion system analysis used across the aerospace community. The modernized CEA code provides critical calculations for rocket performance, shock dynamics, and detonation analysis.

science-space.title: SpaceX launches 29 Starlink satellites, lands rocket on ship at sea
science-space.summary: SpaceX successfully launched 29 Starlink broadband satellites to orbit from Florida's Space Coast and recovered the Falcon 9 rocket booster with a landing on an autonomous drone ship. The mission continues the expansion of the global Starlink satellite internet constellation.

finance-markets.title: Bitcoin and gold surge as Bessent's intervention in bond market hits dollar
finance-markets.summary: Bitcoin and gold rallied sharply following Treasury Secretary Bessent's intervention in the bond market, with bitcoin posting its best week in over three years as investors pursue 'debasement' trades amid currency concerns. The surge reflects broader market concerns about fiscal policy and currency devaluation in response to bond market volatility.

finance-markets.title: The bond scare and the balance of power
finance-markets.summary: Recent bond market volatility signals a return to fundamental concerns about the relationship between fiscal capacity and political power after a decade of monetary abundance. The market turmoil reflects renewed investor scrutiny of government spending and debt sustainability across major economies.

finance-markets.title: US-Canada trade deal goes down to the wire
finance-markets.summary: US-Canada trade negotiations remain unresolved as officials discuss a potential agreement following Trump's pause on $20 billion in new tariffs on the North American trading partner. The ongoing negotiations represent a critical test for continental trade relations and economic stability.

finance-markets.title: Citadel offloads 80% of portfolio scooped up from Situational Awareness
finance-markets.summary: Ken Griffin's Citadel hedge fund has executed over $4 billion in block trades in recent weeks, offloading 80% of a portfolio acquired from Situational Awareness. The large-scale position unwinding reflects significant market activity and portfolio repositioning among major institutional investors.

finance-markets.title: Wall Street Week | AI Hits Wages, USMCA Under Pressure, Colorado River Crisis
finance-markets.summary: Artificial intelligence is beginning to suppress wage growth in exposed occupations despite not yet triggering mass layoffs, while renegotiated USMCA trade terms could create lasting damage to North American manufacturing relationships. The segment also examines critical infrastructure pressures including Colorado River water scarcity affecting regional economic stability.

finance-markets.title: 'Betrayal': US ranchers lash out at Trump's plan to cut tax on beef imports
finance-markets.summary: US ranchers are expressing strong opposition to President Trump's proposal to reduce tariffs on foreign beef imports, claiming the move will undercut domestic producers with cheaper foreign alternatives. The administration has committed to ensuring imported ground beef will sell at 25% below current market prices, sparking agricultural sector backlash.

finance-markets.title: Trump Allows Tariff Relief for Some Ground Beef Imports
finance-markets.summary: President Trump announced tariff relief allowing up to 300,000 metric tons of ground beef imports duty-free for 90 days, with commitments to sell imported beef at 25% below current market prices. The policy aims to provide consumer cost relief while raising concerns among domestic ranchers about market competition.

finance-markets.title: Dow surges 500 points Friday, but index posts back-to-back weekly losses
finance-markets.summary: US stocks rallied on Friday as investors sought stability following steep sell-offs driven by rising Treasury yields, though major indices remain down for consecutive weeks. The mixed performance reflects ongoing market volatility and investor concern over bond market dynamics.

finance-markets.title: Iran's president calls to end war with US from 'position of strength'
finance-markets.summary: Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian signaled openness to resolving tensions with the United States, reflecting internal regime debate over the country's capacity to sustain ongoing economic pressure. The comments suggest potential geopolitical shifts with implications for global energy markets and sanctions policy.

finance-markets.title: Feminism didn't kill the male breadwinner model, the economy did
finance-markets.summary: Economic structural changes rather than social movements have dismantled traditional male-breadwinner family models, with young non-graduate men facing particular economic headwinds in the labor market. The analysis examines how educational and wage disparities have fundamentally altered family economic dynamics.

tech-ai.title: Apple is reportedly cutting hundreds of jobs from Siri, Vision Pro teams
tech-ai.summary: Apple has announced layoffs affecting more than 200 employees working on Siri and Vision Pro initiatives, including the shutdown of a Vision Pro gaming team and reduction of immersive content development. The company stated the changes are intended to evolve its business and deliver better user experiences, though it will create new roles in other areas.

tech-ai.title: TikTok reaches $400M settlement over children's privacy lawsuit
tech-ai.summary: TikTok has agreed to pay $400 million to settle a Department of Justice lawsuit alleging violations of the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act, with $300 million due immediately and $100 million upon final court order. The settlement concludes a two-year legal battle over claims that TikTok collected data from children without parental notification or consent.

tech-ai.title: Nvidia partners with data center developer Cloverleaf
tech-ai.summary: Nvidia has announced a partnership with data center developer Cloverleaf as the semiconductor giant continues aggressive investment in data center infrastructure. The collaboration comes as AI data centers emerge as a significant revenue driver for Nvidia's business.

tech-ai.title: How AI accounting startup Rillet raised $100M and became a unicorn in 48 hours
tech-ai.summary: AI-powered accounting startup Rillet achieved unicorn status in just 48 hours after CEO Nicolas Kopp shared impressive growth metrics at a board meeting, triggering a competitive fundraising frenzy among top-tier investors including Iconiq and Sequoia. The rapid capital raise demonstrates continued investor enthusiasm for AI-driven enterprise software solutions.

tech-ai.title: Anthropic's Opus 4.6 is a smut-machine
tech-ai.summary: Testing by TechCrunch revealed that Anthropic's Claude AI model can be bypassed to generate sexually explicit content despite company policies prohibiting such output. The findings raise concerns about the effectiveness of content safety measures in advanced language models.

tech-ai.title: Nvidia just showed that the harness, not the AI model, is now the real hero
tech-ai.summary: Nvidia research demonstrates that AI agents can achieve strong performance and maintain stability through fine-tuning of system architectures, even when the underlying AI model lacks native proficiency in a task. The findings suggest that implementation design and control mechanisms may be more critical than raw model capability.

tech-ai.title: Walmart is finally adding Apple Pay and Google Pay
tech-ai.summary: Walmart announced it will introduce tap-to-pay functionality through Apple Pay and Google Pay at select locations starting August 24, with full US store rollout expected by year-end 2026 and gas station coverage by mid-2027. The move marks a significant shift for the retail giant, which was among the last major retailers to adopt digital wallet payment methods.

tech-ai.title: Waymo hands over documents in NHTSA's child collision probe
tech-ai.summary: Autonomous vehicle company Waymo has submitted documents to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration as part of an ongoing investigation into child-related collisions involving its vehicles. The responses are currently redacted, with Waymo citing confidential business information protections.

tech-ai.title: Over 1 million people have clicked LinkedIn's AI slop button
tech-ai.summary: LinkedIn reported that over one million users have engaged with its "Seems like AI slop" button introduced in late July, which allows users to flag artificially generated content on the platform. The feature comes after research indicated that approximately 41 percent of LinkedIn's longform posts were detected as fully AI-generated.

tech-ai.title: HoverAir's transforming modular drone has already been halted in the US
tech-ai.summary: The HoverAir Versa, a modular camera device with snap-on drone propeller wings, has ceased accepting US orders just three days after its Indiegogo launch due to FCC drone regulations. The company is now only shipping the camera portion to US backers while halting shipment of the component that transforms it into a drone.

health-biotech.title: RFK Jr. takes another step toward dismantling vaccine recommendations
health-biotech.summary: HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has issued a request for information regarding potential changes to government vaccine recommendations, signaling a policy shift that could affect national immunization standards. The request, which Kennedy clarified is not yet at the draft policymaking stage, seeks feedback on vaccine recommendation categories and testing protocols.

health-biotech.title: STAT+: How a Trump loyalist got the FDA nomination
health-biotech.summary: Heidi Overton has been nominated for a leadership position at the FDA, marking a significant personnel decision in federal drug oversight. The appointment reflects the Trump administration's influence on regulatory agency leadership during its second term.

health-biotech.title: STAT+: FDA approves Ultragenyx gene therapy
health-biotech.summary: The FDA has approved a gene therapy from Ultragenyx for an ultra-rare disease, representing a validating approval for advanced genetic medicine approaches. The decision demonstrates continued regulatory progress in rare disease treatment options.

health-biotech.title: STAT+: Pharmalittle: We're reading about a big Roche investment in the U.S., estrogen patch shortages, and more
health-biotech.summary: Roche's Genentech subsidiary is investing $750 million to expand its drug delivery device production facility in Hillsboro, Oregon, doubling its existing capacity. The investment reflects major pharmaceutical infrastructure development within the United States.

health-biotech.title: China IIT deaths prompt lawmakers to request FDA clampdown
health-biotech.summary: Two Republican lawmakers are urging the FDA to reject clinical data from China unless trial sites have undergone recent agency audits, following deaths in investigational immunotherapy trials. The request signals growing scrutiny of foreign clinical trial data integrity in drug approval processes.

health-biotech.title: As Trump 2.0 targets federal research, a new study shows the stakes
health-biotech.summary: A new study demonstrates that industry has increasingly displaced the federal government as the primary driver of clinical trial research priorities and funding over recent years. The analysis highlights the potential impact of reduced federal research investment on future drug development.

health-biotech.title: Focal therapy for localized prostate cancer has divided physicians. Will new data change minds?
health-biotech.summary: Urologic oncologists remain divided on the clinical benefits of focal therapy compared to traditional surgery or radiation for localized prostate cancer, with emerging data potentially influencing professional consensus. The debate reflects broader questions about treatment intensity and patient outcomes in oncology.

health-biotech.title: How cost and perception could reshape the GLP-1 market
health-biotech.summary: As Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk compete for market dominance in the GLP-1 sector, survey data suggests that drug affordability and physician prescribing preferences will be critical factors in determining competitive outcomes. Cost barriers and perception management may significantly influence market share distribution.

health-biotech.title: Scientists deploy Merck's Ebola vaccine in DRC
health-biotech.summary: Health authorities have begun deploying Merck's Ebola vaccine in the Democratic Republic of Congo as part of an active disease response effort. The vaccination campaign represents a critical public health intervention in infectious disease outbreak control.

health-biotech.title: FDA rejects Osteal combo therapy to treat joint-implant infections
health-biotech.summary: The FDA has rejected Osteal Therapeutics' combination therapy designed to treat bacterial and microbial infections around joint implants, requiring the company to pursue additional development or reformulation. The setback represents a challenge in addressing a significant clinical problem in orthopedic surgery.

startups-vc.title: How AI accounting startup Rillet raised $100M and became a unicorn in 48 hours
startups-vc.summary: AI accounting startup Rillet achieved unicorn status within 48 hours after CEO Nicolas Kopp shared impressive growth metrics at a board meeting, triggering a fundraising frenzy from top-tier investors including Iconiq and Sequoia. The rapid milestone demonstrates exceptional market demand and investor enthusiasm for AI-powered enterprise software solutions.

startups-vc.title: Why is the DOJ investigating Andreessen Horowitz's board seats?
startups-vc.summary: The Department of Justice has been investigating Andreessen Horowitz for nearly a year regarding potential antitrust violations, specifically over board seat conflicts where a16z partners Ben Horowitz and Martin Casado serve on competing companies Databricks and Fivetran. The investigation invokes a rarely-used 112-year-old antitrust law and could have significant implications for how venture capital firms manage portfolio company board governance.

startups-vc.title: VCs Pour Billions Into Physical AI As The Next Wave Of AI Investing Takes Shape
startups-vc.summary: Venture capital funding in the physical AI sector surged to $47.4 billion across 521 deals in the first half of 2026, representing nearly a fourfold increase from the second half of 2025 when the sector raised $12 billion. This dramatic acceleration indicates physical AI and robotics have become a major focus area for institutional venture investors globally.

startups-vc.title: Starcloud raises $250 million for orbital data centers as launch options dry up
startups-vc.summary: Orbital infrastructure startup Starcloud secured $250 million in funding to develop data centers in space as traditional launch capacity becomes increasingly constrained. The substantial financing reflects growing investor conviction in the commercial potential of space-based computing infrastructure.

startups-vc.title: The Week's 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Defense Tech, AI Tools And Infrastructure Lead The Way
startups-vc.summary: Defense technology, artificial intelligence infrastructure, and data center companies dominated the week's largest funding rounds, with Castelion, a hypersonic missile developer, securing the largest financing. The funding patterns underscore investor prioritization of defense technology, AI inference capabilities, and physical infrastructure across the startup ecosystem.

startups-vc.title: ServiceTitan Just Shut Off Podium's Integration for ~1,000 Shared Customers
startups-vc.summary: ServiceTitan terminated its nine-year integration partnership with Podium, affecting approximately 1,000 shared customers during peak HVAC season, after Podium developed competing agent-based technology. The abrupt decision illustrates how AI-driven product competition is reshaping long-standing SaaS partnerships and strategic alliances.

startups-vc.title: Harshita Arora Joins YC as General Partner
startups-vc.summary: Y Combinator announced Harshita Arora as a new General Partner, bringing extensive fintech and infrastructure expertise along with early-stage founder experience. Her appointment strengthens YC's investment capabilities in critical sectors and underscores the firm's commitment to deepening domain expertise within its partnership.

startups-vc.title: Runlayer, Rippling drop lawsuits — but the brouhaha is still a cautionary tale for founders
startups-vc.summary: Runlayer and Rippling settled their legal dispute without monetary damages, though Rippling subsequently launched a competing product. The incident serves as a cautionary example for founders regarding intellectual property disputes and competitive dynamics in the SaaS market.

startups-vc.title: 5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: AI For Everything From Recycling To Breathing To Winning Construction Bids
startups-vc.summary: This month's overview highlights diverse artificial intelligence applications across verticals including waste management, healthcare, and commercial real estate prospecting. The range of AI-focused deals demonstrates the technology's broad enterprise and consumer applicability beyond traditional software categories.

startups-vc.title: Adding Canada Back to Our List of Accepted Countries of Incorporation
startups-vc.summary: Y Combinator restored Canada to its list of accepted countries of incorporation following feedback from its Canadian founder community. The decision reflects YC's commitment to supporting the Canadian startup ecosystem and expanding geographic accessibility to its accelerator program.

crypto-web3.title: Washington Goes All-In on Crypto: Trump Pushes Clarity, SEC Rules, and CFTC Warnings
crypto-web3.summary: The Trump administration is accelerating crypto regulation efforts, with the president urging passage of a fair version of the Clarity Act while the CFTC threatened to establish its own rules if Congress stalls. The SEC simultaneously advanced its first crypto fundraising framework, signaling a major shift in Washington's regulatory approach to digital assets.

crypto-web3.title: The hard truth is that the Clarity Act is an anti-crypto bill
crypto-web3.summary: Berkeley Law lecturer Hermine Wong argues that despite industry hunger for comprehensive crypto legislation, the Clarity Act represents a political trap that undermines digital asset innovation rather than protecting it. The critique challenges the narrative that any regulation is preferable to continued regulatory uncertainty.

crypto-web3.title: Crypto advocates join in suing Illinois over digital asset tax
crypto-web3.summary: The Crypto Council for Innovation and the Blockchain Association have filed a lawsuit challenging Illinois's newly approved 0.2% tax on digital asset transactions. The legal action represents coordinated industry resistance to state-level crypto taxation policies.

crypto-web3.title: Wall Street and Washington Fuel Bitcoin Rally: Here's What's Going On
crypto-web3.summary: Bitcoin's surge is being driven by institutional buying, improving macroeconomic conditions, and a more favorable regulatory environment, with billions in short liquidations accelerating the price movement. The convergence of Wall Street interest and Washington policy signals suggests sustained momentum in the digital asset market.

crypto-web3.title: Nomura-backed Laser Digital wins Japan's first crypto approval in four years
crypto-web3.summary: Laser Digital Japan has secured regulatory approval to offer liquidity services to domestic cryptocurrency providers, marking Japan's first major crypto license in four years. The development reflects growing institutional appetite for digital assets and Japan's renewed openness to the crypto sector.

crypto-web3.title: Coldcard ships firmware after $114 million bitcoin theft; says AI helped catch more bugs
crypto-web3.summary: Hardware wallet manufacturer Coldcard has released a firmware update following a $114 million theft exploit, disclosing that a three-week security review using AI uncovered additional vulnerabilities beyond the original flaw. The company warns that updates alone cannot secure previously compromised wallets.

crypto-web3.title: Bitcoin ETFs Just Had Their Biggest Day Since May—BlackRock Took 83% of It
crypto-web3.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs attracted $606 million on Thursday, the largest single day inflow since May, with BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust capturing the majority of inflows. The surge reflects renewed institutional interest in cryptocurrency investment products alongside altcoin fund inflows.

crypto-web3.title: Bitcoin tops $77,000 as best week since 2023 pulls altcoins along for the ride
crypto-web3.summary: Bitcoin has surged 24% since Monday to exceed $77,000, achieving a price level implied by the breakdown of an inverse head-and-shoulders technical pattern while dragging altcoins higher. Despite the rally, short positions remain contrarian, suggesting further potential upside.

crypto-web3.title: Most Americans Say Trump's Crypto Profits Cross the Line: Poll
crypto-web3.summary: A Reuters/Ipsos survey found that 63% of Americans view the Trump family's cryptocurrency holdings and profits as inappropriate, with even half of Republican respondents questioning whether the president's business interests influence his regulatory decisions. The polling suggests potential political headwinds for aggressive pro-crypto policy.

crypto-web3.title: Solana Just Got Faster—Is It Bullish for SOL?
crypto-web3.summary: Solana has activated its first reduction in block timing since network launch, increasing transaction speed on the blockchain. The network upgrade could enhance user experience and potentially support price appreciation for the SOL token.

cybersecurity.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
cybersecurity.summary: A 26-year-old Canadian cybercriminal has pleaded guilty to hacking and extorting over 165 organizations using Snowflake's cloud data platform, representing one of the most consequential cyber threats of 2024. The defendant also admitted to stealing call and text records from more than 100 million AT&T customers, demonstrating the massive scale of data compromise affecting both enterprises and consumers.

cybersecurity.title: Microsoft Defender's Own Driver Can Be Weaponized to Delete Security Software at Boot
cybersecurity.summary: Check Point Research disclosed a critical technique exploiting Microsoft Defender's legitimately signed BTR.sys driver to perform arbitrary kernel-level operations across Windows 7 through Windows 11 25H2 without requiring any software flaw or external driver. This vulnerability enables attackers to weaponize built-in security infrastructure to undermine system defenses at the most critical boot stage.

cybersecurity.title: GitLab CVE-2026-19478 Comes Under Active Exploitation Within Days of Disclosure
cybersecurity.summary: A code injection vulnerability in GitLab (CVE-2026-19478, CVSS 9.4) is being actively exploited in the wild within days of public disclosure, allowing unauthenticated attackers to modify or delete publicly accessible projects and rewrite their data. The rapid exploitation timeline underscores the critical urgency for organizations to patch this flaw immediately.

cybersecurity.title: Microsoft Patches Severe Entra ID Flaw (CVSS 10.0) Allowing Remote Code Execution
cybersecurity.summary: Microsoft released a patch for a critical Entra ID vulnerability with a CVSS score of 10.0 that could enable remote code execution, though the company later clarified that exploitation has not been observed in the wild. Organizations should prioritize patching this maximum-severity flaw to prevent potential compromise of identity and access management systems.

cybersecurity.title: 14 Trojanized npm Packages Drop RedC2 4.0 Linux Backdoor With AI-Assisted C2
cybersecurity.summary: Researchers discovered 14 malicious npm packages masquerading as legitimate calendar and utility tools that deliver RedC2 4.0, an AI-powered Linux backdoor with sophisticated command and control capabilities. The supply chain attack leverages the npm ecosystem's trust to distribute advanced persistent backdoors to developers.

cybersecurity.title: Cisco Patches Nine Crosswork and Secure Workload Flaws, Five Scoring CVSS 10.0
cybersecurity.summary: Cisco released patches for nine vulnerabilities affecting its Crosswork platforms and Secure Workload software, with five flaws achieving the maximum CVSS severity score of 10.0. The updates continue Cisco's comprehensive internal security review and address critical infrastructure risks across multiple Crosswork products.

cybersecurity.title: Lessons Learned from CISA's Recent GitHub Leak
cybersecurity.summary: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency published a postmortem on a significant data leak where a contractor exposed dozens of internal CISA credentials, including AWS Govcloud keys, in a public GitHub repository for six months. Security experts highlight critical lessons from the incident response gaps that all organizations' security teams should implement.

cybersecurity.title: Android Car Malware Spreads Through Built-In Updaters for Ad Fraud, Proxy Botnet
cybersecurity.summary: Kaspersky researchers discovered a new malware family targeting Android-based vehicle infotainment systems developed by DoFun, spreading through built-in firmware update mechanisms to enable ad fraud and proxy botnet creation. The attack represents a novel vector targeting connected vehicle infrastructure with operational impact on both fleet management and user privacy.

cybersecurity.title: N-able Bug Exposes Password Vault Master Keys
cybersecurity.summary: A vulnerability in N-able's popular Passportal password manager, widely adopted by managed service providers and small-to-medium businesses, exposes master encryption keys due to inherent risks in its cloud-based architecture. Security experts question whether sensitive password management tools should remain in cloud infrastructure given the elevated exposure risks.

cybersecurity.title: LG to Ban Residential Proxies from Smart TV Apps
cybersecurity.summary: LG Electronics USA announced plans to suspend smart TV apps that convert televisions into always-on residential proxy nodes following research revealing that over 42 percent of webOS store applications permitted unknown third parties to route internet traffic through users' devices. The action addresses a significant privacy and security vulnerability in consumer IoT devices that could facilitate botnet operations.

energy-climate.title: Q&A: What is in China's new five-year plan for climate change?
energy-climate.summary: China has released its 15th five-year plan dedicated to addressing climate change, outlining comprehensive national strategies for emissions reduction and climate adaptation. The plan represents a major policy framework from the world's largest emitter and signals China's climate commitments through 2030.

energy-climate.title: Analysis: Weaker EV targets could cost UK consumers £3bn a year by 2030
energy-climate.summary: A proposed UK government consultation on weakening electric vehicle targets could impose significant financial costs on consumers, amounting to approximately £3 billion annually by 2030. The analysis highlights the economic implications of delaying EV adoption targets in a major developed economy.

energy-climate.title: China's Jiangsu province crosses 100 GW solar milestone
energy-climate.summary: Jiangsu Province in eastern China has become the country's first provincial-level region to exceed 100 GW of installed solar PV capacity, with distributed solar accounting for nearly 70% of the total. The province plans accelerated expansion through 2030 and 2035 with corresponding upgrades to grid infrastructure and energy storage systems.

energy-climate.title: Q&A: Does the world need 'carbon capture and storage' to reach net-zero?
energy-climate.summary: The article examines the role of carbon capture and storage technology in achieving global net-zero emissions targets, assessing whether CCS is a necessary component of climate mitigation strategies. It provides analysis of the technology's potential contribution to decarbonization pathways.

energy-climate.title: Final caisson installed at 3.5GW Princess Elisabeth Energy Island project
energy-climate.summary: The installation of all 23 caissons for the Princess Elisabeth Energy Island, a major offshore wind infrastructure project, has been completed 45 kilometers off the Belgian coast in the North Sea. The project represents significant progress in large-scale offshore renewable energy development.

energy-climate.title: Austria announces energy storage offensive, shifting solar subsidy focus
energy-climate.summary: Austria is overhauling its solar subsidy framework from 2027 to prioritize battery storage and energy management systems alongside specialized solar applications. The government aims to deploy up to 8 GW of market-oriented storage capacity by 2030, signaling a strategic shift toward grid-scale energy storage.

energy-climate.title: Ørsted plans 2GW Dadu 2 offshore wind project in Taiwan
energy-climate.summary: Ørsted has announced plans for the Dadu 2 offshore wind project in Taiwan with a planned capacity of up to 2 gigawatts. The project expands renewable energy development in the Asia-Pacific region and supports Taiwan's clean energy transition goals.

energy-climate.title: Explainer: How the 'super El Niño' will reshape the world's weather
energy-climate.summary: The world is currently experiencing what is expected to become the strongest El Niño on record, dubbed a 'super El Niño,' which will have significant impacts on global weather patterns. The phenomenon has direct implications for climate volatility and extreme weather events worldwide.

energy-climate.title: Utility-scale projects drive New Zealand's solar rollout
energy-climate.summary: New Zealand achieved record solar capacity additions in 2025, driven primarily by the commissioning of seven utility-scale plants, with an additional 930 MW expected to come online over the next three years. The growth demonstrates accelerating renewable energy deployment in the Southern Hemisphere.

energy-climate.title: Mitsubishi Electric to buy US-based PCI Energy Solutions for $1.4bn
energy-climate.summary: Mitsubishi Electric has agreed to acquire PCI Energy Solutions, a US-based energy company, in a transaction valued at $1.4 billion. The acquisition signals strategic expansion by a major Japanese electronics manufacturer into the North American energy solutions sector.

asia-pacific.title: China and US push Southeast Asia over their AI blocs. Will it test region's non-alignment?
asia-pacific.summary: The United States and China are competing to align Southeast Asian nations with their respective artificial intelligence ecosystems, with Washington promoting its China-free 'Pax Silica' supply chain while Beijing advances its World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organisation. This technological rivalry threatens to test Southeast Asia's traditional stance of non-alignment between the two great powers.

asia-pacific.title: China's Own Version of Ambiguity in the Taiwan Strait
asia-pacific.summary: China is reportedly shifting its pressure campaign in the Taiwan Strait away from highly visible military coercion toward less easily classified methods as the United States debates adopting 'strategic clarity' in its Taiwan policy. This strategic shift reflects Beijing's evolving approach to cross-strait tensions.

asia-pacific.title: Malaysia's Anwar traded reform for power. Now Umno wants it all
asia-pacific.summary: Malaysia's ruling People's Justice Party (PKR) and Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim face growing political pressure from the opposition United Malays National Organisation (Umno), which is demanding concessions after three years of the government's reform agenda. The article examines tensions within Malaysia's coalition government over the balance between institutional reform and political power consolidation.

asia-pacific.title: Australia and Thailand Deepen Ties to Hedge Against Global Uncertainty
asia-pacific.summary: Australia and Thailand are strengthening bilateral collaboration as a strategic response to regional uncertainties and shifting geopolitical dynamics. This partnership deepening is part of Australia's broader long-term vision for Indo-Pacific engagement.

asia-pacific.title: TikTok, ByteDance agree to US$400 million settlement with US over children's privacy suit
asia-pacific.summary: TikTok and its parent company ByteDance have agreed to pay $400 million to settle a Justice Department and Federal Trade Commission lawsuit alleging violations of children's online privacy laws. The settlement represents a major resolution in a case that has been subject to intense political scrutiny regarding the platform's American operations.

asia-pacific.title: How an Academic Became Collateral Damage to China's Interests in Myanmar
asia-pacific.summary: The arrest of Burmese-American scholar U Min Zin underscores China's determination to prevent scrutiny of its strategic interests and role in Myanmar's internal affairs. The case illustrates China's willingness to pursue individuals who may threaten its geopolitical positioning in the country.

asia-pacific.title: How Mongolia Is Diversifying Its Defense Sector
asia-pacific.summary: Mongolia is expanding its defense industry capabilities through partnerships with Turkey, as exemplified by a new ammunition manufacturing facility. This diversification effort reflects Mongolia's strategic efforts to strengthen its defense capabilities beyond traditional partnerships.

asia-pacific.title: Can Bangladesh Engage the Arakan Army Without Compromising Rohingya Rights?
asia-pacific.summary: Bangladesh faces the challenge of engaging with the Arakan Army armed group while protecting the interests and rights of Rohingya refugees on its territory. The article examines the delicate balance between necessary dialogue with non-state actors and maintaining humanitarian commitments.

asia-pacific.title: A New Japanese Drydock and the Limits of Allied Cooperation
asia-pacific.summary: Japanese shipyards are undergoing expansion; however, future capacity appears to be already committed or constrained within existing allied arrangements. The article examines the limitations of defense industrial cooperation within the US-Japan alliance framework.

asia-pacific.title: The US is telling its trading partners – do as I say, not as I do
asia-pacific.summary: A US Treasury Department report on the macroeconomic and foreign exchange policies of major trading partners reveals inconsistencies in American positions on currency intervention and trade practices. The analysis highlights the gap between US prescriptions for other nations and its own economic policy approaches.
